Duluth Ore Dock Company
TypeIron-ore dock operator (invented for this demo)
LocationDuluth, Minnesota
Known docksDock No. 6
Family membersAnders Calder (dock foreman); Henrik Calder (chute tender)

The Duluth Ore Dock Company is the employer named on the 1938 payroll ledger in this demonstration lineage. Ore trains ran out along the top of its docks and dropped iron ore through chutes into the boats below.[1][2]

The Calders at the dock

In October 1938 the payroll for Dock No. 6 listed Anders Calder as dock foreman and his son Henrik Calder as chute tender.[3] Henrik's daughter Ruth Calder remembered the dock as so tall "you had to tip your head all the way back," with the trains running "right out on top of it."[2]

History

A 1925 history of the docks at the head of Lake Superior, now in the public domain, describes the company's timber and steel docks and their chutes.[1]
